title: Make another coffee of the same kind: bin the stuck used capsule, then load a new capsule of the same colour from memory
instruction: Make another coffee of the same kind. First take the used capsule out of the coffee machine's holder and drop it into the green recycling tin through the hole in its lid: the used capsule sticks, so hold the machine down by its water tank with your other hand while you pull it out. Only once it is in the tin, take the new capsule of the same kind, the same colour, as the used one from the wooden tray, put it in the holder, and press the brew button. Do not take any other capsule. Then take both arms back to where they started.
context: Making a drink the way someone likes it again is an everyday household task for an assistant. It also tests memory: once the used capsule has slid out of sight inside the tin, nothing in view says which kind it was, and the three new capsules differ only in colour.
setup: A table in front of two arms (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them. (1) A capsule coffee machine (0.3 kg in simulation, ABS and steel), standing loose on the table: a black body 12 cm deep, 25 cm wide and 7 cm tall with a charcoal top, its middle 31.5 cm forward and 2.5 cm left of the centre line. In its top on the right, a capsule holder: a square opening 7.2 cm across with a 1.2 cm deep pocket and a brushed steel trim ring; at its left end a clear blue water tank 7 x 5 x 4.5 cm with a tinted lid; a round brew button 2.4 cm across, 3.5 cm in front of its middle; a spout at its front, a steel drip tray and a white cup 4.8 cm across on it. (2) In the holder, a used blue capsule, stuck: it comes free only under a pull of 6 N, while the machine weighs 2.9 N. (3) A beech tray 20 x 8 cm, fixed, 19.5 cm right of the centre line, holding three new capsules (each 5.6 cm across the rim, 3.4 cm tall, 30 g, aluminium with a foil lid): red 26.5 cm forward, gold 32.5 cm, blue 38.5 cm. (4) A green steel recycling tin for used capsules, fixed: 15.8 x 9.8 cm and 8.9 cm tall, its middle 33 cm forward and 34.5 cm right of the centre line, with a square hole 6.6 cm across in the back part of its lid; a slick ramp inside slides a dropped capsule forward under the solid front part of the lid, out of sight. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: A capsule counts as taken once it has moved more than 1.5 cm from its place on the tray. The used capsule is in the tin once it is inside the tin's walls, below its lid. The new capsule is seated once its middle is within 1.8 cm of the holder's middle, its underside within 8 mm of the pocket's floor, and it is tilted at most 15 degrees. The coffee is brewed when a gripper's fingertip centre comes within 2.2 cm (sideways) and 1.2 cm (above) of the brew button's top while the blue capsule is seated: the button lights, coffee runs from the spout for 3 s and the cup fills. The score is 0.0 once a red or gold capsule was taken, and 0.0 once the blue one was taken before the used capsule was in the tin. Otherwise 1.0: the coffee brewed, the blue capsule still seated, the machine standing on the table (lifted less than 4 mm, tilted less than 3 degrees), and both arms back where they started (each gripper's fingertip centre within 5 cm of its start); 0.75: the coffee brewed; 0.5: the blue capsule seated; 0.25: the used capsule in the tin; else 0.0. Judged at the end of the trial, which ends at the run limit, or once the full score has held for 1 s with the machine and the capsule still.
reset_notes: Put the used (blue) capsule back in the holder (it is stuck there again at every reset), the three new capsules on the tray, and the machine in its place; the cup is empty again.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1, PhysX, 20 Hz control). Simplified: the capsules are about 1.5 times real size so the grippers can hold them; the used capsule is held by a joint that breaks under 6 N; brewing is a rule (button press with the capsule seated), and the button light, coffee stream and filling cup are drawn shapes. The machine is 0.3 kg, light enough to lift with the capsule unless held down.
